latest_lesson.topic_title: Navigating Office Small Talk and Networking
latest_lesson.article: In today’s fast-paced workplace, mastering small talk is more than just being friendly; it is a key skill for career growth. Whether you are grabbing coffee in the breakroom or waiting for a meeting to start, these short interactions build rapport with colleagues. However, many professionals feel nervous about what to say. If you are ever unsure, try asking open-ended questions like, 'How has your week been so far?' or 'What are you working on these days?' These simple prompts invite others to share more than just a 'yes' or 'no' answer. Furthermore, not only do these conversations help you network, but they also make the office environment more enjoyable. Never underestimate the power of a casual chat. Rarely do we realize how much a five-minute conversation can influence our professional relationships. By practicing these skills, you will eventually find it much easier to connect with people from different departments. Remember, the goal is not to be perfect, but to be genuine. So, next time you see a coworker, take a deep breath and start a conversation. It is a small step that can lead to big opportunities in your career journey.

vocabulary.example: It is important to build a good rapport with your new colleagues during your first week.
Try to ask open-ended questions to keep the conversation flowing naturally.
Do not underestimate the impact of a positive attitude in the workplace.
People appreciate it when you show a genuine interest in their work.
The project was not only challenging but also very rewarding for the team.

podcast_script.speaker: Alex
podcast_script.text: Hey Maya, I was reading this article about office small talk. Do you find it hard to start conversations with coworkers?

podcast_script.speaker: Maya
podcast_script.text: Honestly, Alex, sometimes I do! Especially when I'm busy. How about you?

podcast_script.speaker: Alex
podcast_script.text: Same here. But the article says it’s actually a key skill for networking. It’s not just about passing time.

podcast_script.speaker: Maya
podcast_script.text: That makes sense. I guess it helps build rapport, right? It makes the office feel less formal.

podcast_script.speaker: Alex
podcast_script.text: Exactly. The article suggests using open-ended questions. Like, instead of saying 'Is your day busy?', ask 'What are you working on?'

podcast_script.speaker: Maya
podcast_script.text: Oh, that’s a great tip. Not only does that keep the talk going, but it also shows you care about their tasks.

podcast_script.speaker: Alex
podcast_script.text: Spot on. And rarely do we think about how those five minutes can actually help our careers later on.

podcast_script.speaker: Maya
podcast_script.text: True. I’ll definitely try to be more genuine next time I’m at the coffee machine!

comprehension_quiz.question: According to the article, why should you use open-ended questions?
options: To finish the conversation as quickly as possible.
To get more detailed answers from your colleagues.
To test if your coworkers are listening to you.
To avoid talking about work-related topics.
comprehension_quiz.explanation_zh: 文章提到使用開放式問題（open-ended questions）的目的是鼓勵對方分享更多資訊，而非僅回答簡單的「是」或「否」。

comprehension_quiz.question: Which of the following is true about small talk based on the text?
options: It is only useful for people who are new to the company.
It usually makes the office environment feel more stressful.
It can positively influence your professional relationships.
It should always be strictly about professional tasks.
comprehension_quiz.explanation_zh: 文章強調閒聊（small talk）能幫助建立職場人際關係，並讓辦公室氛圍更融洽。
